top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a mature, reproduced advance: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye's realisation of many-atom interrogation near 1e-18, independently matched at several national laboratories. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation can be scoped to the lattice scheme so it is distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. I accept that a clock's redefinition and fundamental-physics payoffs are still prospective. P002 is a genuine prediction-then-observation arc, but the three-name cap leaves out the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Hasan's 3D work, and it overlaps the 2016 topological-phases prize, so the credit is weaker than for P001. It still ranks above no award, which I would use only if no defensible allocation existed.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as a theorist in electronic-structure and magnetism I have no documented connection to the lattice-clock laureates, and the topological-insulator work is only a field-adjacent interest
